title: Wrap-up: loops that stop
idea: Review: progress, boundaries, zero-time loops, and choosing for vs while.

exercises.prompt: Match each idea to its meaning (a review of this unit).

pairs.right: Each pass moves toward the stop
Runs one time too many or too few
Condition false at the start, body skipped

exercises.explanation: These four ideas cover making a loop stop correctly: ending, moving, counting, and the empty case.

exercises.prompt:
What shows?

i = 1
while i <= 3:
    print(i)
    i = i + 1
exercises.explanation: i is 1,2,3; at i = 4 the condition is false. The update i = i + 1 makes it stop -- a safe loop.
The first grows i while checking i > 0 -- always true. The last runs zero times; the middle two stop.

exercises.prompt: A while loop checks its condition before each pass, so it can run zero times.
exercises.explanation: True. If the condition starts false, the body is skipped entirely -- a safe and sometimes useful outcome.

exercises.prompt: You need to repeat exactly 8 times. Best loop?
exercises.explanation: A known count is a for-loop: range(8) runs exactly eight times with no update to forget.

exercises.prompt: You keep asking until the input is valid. Best loop?
exercises.explanation: An unknown number of tries, decided by a condition, is a while loop.

exercises.prompt: Arrange a safe countdown that prints 3, 2, 1 and stops.
exercises.explanation: Setup n = 3, condition n > 0, print, update n = n - 1. Shrinking n reaches 0 and stops the loop.
% gives the remainder. i % 2 == 0 is true when i divides evenly by 2 -- an even number.

exercises.prompt:
How many numbers does this print?

i = 2
while i < 10:
    print(i)
    i = i + 2
exercises.explanation: i is 2,4,6,8 then 10 fails 10 < 10. Four numbers. Adding 2 each pass still makes progress to the stop.

exercises.prompt: The big idea of this unit in one line:
options: Every while loop needs progress toward its condition becoming false
exercises.explanation: Make sure each pass moves toward the stop, watch the boundary, and your loops will always end. Next: stopping or skipping mid-loop!
